title: Stitch: "that's just a skinny crocodile"

scenes.headline: Close. It's a gharial. Look at the snout.
scenes.body: Long and slender, built for catching fish.

scenes.label: Razor-sharp teeth in a gharial's jaws

scenes.headline: Critically Endangered (IUCN)
scenes.body: Males grow a bulb on the snout tip, the 'ghara', used in courtship.

caption:
Not a crocodile. Not a skinny one either.

Gharials historically lived in four river systems: the Indus, Ganges, Mahanadi and Brahmaputra. As they age, their snouts get longer and they eat almost only fish.

Source: Animal Diversity Web.  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Stitch demo answering a common misconception; in real use the first beat is the other creator's reel via native Stitch. Media thin: one gharial photo, plus a Nile crocodile clip (Nairobi NP) for comparison.
